about: How the two METRIC readers decode the bytes of a run's output: dev-spec-driven's stream reader (done --run and finish --run) and dev-guardian's file reader (the metrics command). Written once, kept byte-identical in both repositories, each suite pinning its sha256. A change is metric-bytes/2, a new file landed in both before either tags. The lines themselves are metric-lines/1's. An absent value is null, never a missing key.

modes.stream: dev-spec-driven: stdout and stderr read apart, each decoded as UTF-8 (an invalid byte read as U+FFFD), one leading U+FEFF of each dropped, then read as two texts in that order: a name on both reads stderr's line
modes.file: dev-guardian metrics --head: one file, the two streams in print order (a 2>&1 capture); its last readBytes bytes read (fileReadBytes when set); UTF-16 by a byte-order mark, or by NUL-interleaved bytes at the start of what is read (the check --file rule), else UTF-8 with its byte-order mark dropped; the last printed line of a name wins

fields.stdout: the bytes the run wrote to stdout, lowercase hex
fields.stderr: the bytes it wrote to stderr, lowercase hex
fields.printed: stdout or stderr: the stream a 2>&1 capture holds first (the file is the two concatenated in that order)
fields.fileReadBytes: null, or the bytes of the file's end the file reader reads in place of readBytes (the read bound, at a size a fixture can hold)
fields.file: the file reader's reading: metrics (each name kept: value, unit, better, tolerance) in the order of the file's lines, repeats, malformed, dropped, as metric-lines/1's outputs
fields.stream: the stream reader's reading, the same shape: metrics in the order of stdout's lines, then stderr's
fields.differs: null when the two readings are equal, else why they are not: a decision, never an accident

cases.note: a UTF-8 byte-order mark at the output's start (a Windows tool writing UTF-8 with one, CRLF ends): dropped, the first line read

cases.differs: the stream reader drops one leading byte-order mark of each stream; the file holds the stream printed second with its mark mid-file, where no line starts
cases.note: a tool writing a byte-order mark on each stream, stderr printed first (a program whose stdout is buffered when it is no terminal)
a mark after a line break inside one stream (a child writing into the same pipe): no line starts there, in either reader
one mark is dropped, a second one stays

cases.differs: the file reader reads UTF-16 by its byte-order mark; the stream reader decodes a stream as UTF-8
cases.note: what Windows PowerShell 5.1's > and Out-File write

cases.differs: the file reader guesses UTF-16 from NUL-interleaved bytes; the stream reader decodes a stream as UTF-8
the file reader reads the end of a file past its read bound, where no byte-order mark is, and guesses UTF-16 there; the stream reader decodes a stream as UTF-8
cases.note: a UTF-16 file longer than the file reader's read bound (fileReadBytes stands for readBytes)
UTF-16LE text with no mark (wsl.exe's own messages) then a UTF-8 line: the file reader decodes it all as UTF-16; the stream reader sees a NUL before the keyword, after the head's last line break

cases.differs: the file reader decodes the whole file as UTF-16 when its start is NUL-interleaved; the stream reader decodes UTF-8 and reads the line after the NULs
cases.note: a NUL-interleaved head with no NUL after its last line break, then a UTF-8 line
binary with NULs on both sides of the byte pairs (small 32-bit integers) is never guessed UTF-16

cases.differs: the stream reader reads stdout, then stderr, so stderr's line of a name wins; the file holds the two streams in print order, the last printed winning
cases.note: a name printed on both streams
